24 
National African American Read-In 
On Thursday, February 19, 2026, UMass Dartmouth hosted its 
Annual National African American Read-In, a celebration of 
African American literature and storytelling. The event brought 
together students, faculty, staff, and community members to 
honor and share the works of African American authors, poets, 
and spoken-word artists. 
Participants had the opportunity to read selections from their 
favorite works or listen as others presented meaningful and 
inspiring pieces, creating a shared experience that highlighted 
the richness and impact of African American voices. 
The event featured a poetry reading and book signing by 
Gail Gonsalves (G.G. Cosmos), a poet and author from New 
Bedford, Massachusetts, whose published works include   Long 
Time Comin’   (2023),   Just Saying!   (2023),   The Space Between Us 
(2024), and the co-authored   Love Jams, Affirmations of Sweet 
Nothings   (2025) with Tracy Macleod (@LotusArt33). Through her 
readings and reflections, attendees were able to engage with 
her creative journey, gaining insight into the inspiration behind 
her work and connecting with themes of self-expression, 
resilience, faith, love, and service woven throughout her writing. 
The Read-In was made possible through the sponsorship of the 
Leduc Center for Civic Engagement, Frederick Douglass Unity 
House, the Office of Diversity, Equity & Inclusion, the Division 
of Student Affairs and Black History 4 Seasons Council. We 
also extend our sincere gratitude to the Claire T. Carney Library 
Dean, Nancy Goldeski, for curating a selection of books that 
attendees could explore and enjoy throughout the event.
